evidence.explanation: Direct C RNG edges are delegated through levelTrapEnv.random in both JS trap-type selectors. These five edges share one delegation cause; supplied legal draw values produce the same results and checked draw bounds/counts in the finite domain.
evidence.proof: 7000 exact-C/general-JS selector comparisons:25 initial trap choices ×7 secondary values ×10 contexts (ordinary depths1..8, hell depth26, one-level Knox depth18) ×noteleport0/1 ×NOSPIDERONWEB0/4. Results match, including2746 NO_TRAP returns,4254 accepted choices and280 hole cases making a second rn2(7) call. Exact C bodies and trap enum are included; C level predicates use asserted context adapters. JS uses production level_difficulty and single_level_branch with explicit minimal dungeon state.
evidence.control: All seven legal Rogue rn2(7) choices match exact C and each uses one draw. General matrix includes accepted and rejected threshold/flag controls. This is helper-contract evidence, not trap construction, whole dungeon-state equivalence, independent RNG, retry/placement or runtime effects.
